body:
Marcus Reed: quick q while wiring the prefill/decode separation hooks (re: PR-24857). where exactly are we drawing the line between “prefill scheduling” vs “decode scheduling” in the runtime? i’m trying to avoid long-prefill grabbing the whole batch and causing HOL.

Marcus Reed: i see `Scheduler::select_batch()` currently just pulls from the single pending queue and then the executor figures out prefill vs decode on the fly. do we want two passes? (prefill candidates first, then decode fill?) or two distinct queues in this refactor?

Lena Fischer: we’re not going full two-queue in this PR, just separation points so the next PR can do class queues cleanly.

Lena Fischer: code pointers:
- `runtime/serving/scheduler/scheduler.cc` -> `build_iteration_plan()` is where we decide what *types* of work to put into the next GPU iteration.
- `runtime/serving/scheduler/request_state.h` has `Phase { PREFILL, DECODE }` (new-ish).
- in this PR we’re adding `eligible_for_prefill_dispatch()` vs `eligible_for_decode_dispatch()` helpers, so selection logic doesn’t treat them interchangeably.

Lena Fischer: the “line” is basically: if `generated_tokens == 0` and `prompt_tokens > 0` => PREFILL; otherwise DECODE. (we’ll refine w/ speculative + tool calls later but ignore for prototype)

Marcus Reed: got it. so for this PR we expose phase so that batching can avoid mixing too much prefill into decode iteration?

Omar El-Sayed: +1. main thing is KV cache allocation/locking is different. prefill wants to allocate KV blocks sized to prompt, decode wants to reuse + append. if scheduler treats both as identical, prefill will happily starve decode bc it “looks” like high work but the queue doesn’t know.

Omar El-Sayed: watch for this footgun: if you pick a bunch of PREFILL requests into an iteration, you can blow the per-iter KV alloc budget and then decode requests get pushed out even if they’re already hot.

Marcus Reed: makes sense. where do we plumb the per-iteration token budget? i saw notes about keeping prefill capped.

Lena Fischer: token budget guardrails land in PR-24872, but you can keep this PR compatible by:
- ensuring `IterationPlan` has two counters (`prefill_tokens_planned`, `decode_tokens_planned`)
- and a cheap clamp like `max_prefill_tokens_per_iter` (even if config default is “infinite” for now)

Benji Okafor: config naming FYI (from the earlier thread):
- `scheduler.prefill.max_tokens_per_iter`
- `scheduler.decode.max_tokens_per_iter`
- `scheduler.enable_prefill_decode_separation` (flag)
we can bikeshed later but pls don’t invent a 4th name :)

Marcus Reed: lol ok. will use those.

Hiro Tanaka: kernel-side: be careful if you’re alternating heavy prefill iterations with decode-heavy iterations. we’ve seen “kernel thrash” where autotuner keeps reselecting GEMM/attention kernels bc shapes swing between long seq prefill and short seq decode.

Hiro Tanaka: if you can, keep the iteration plan “decode-first” once there’s an active decode backlog. don’t flip flop iteration composition every tick.

Yuki Sato: +1 to Hiro. if you do phase-aware selection, please also keep shapes stable:
- prefer keeping a fixed `max_prefill_batch` or `prefill_token_cap`
- avoid mixing 8k prompt prefills with 128-token decode in same step (it triggers different attention paths)

Grace Kim: perf sanity check suggestion: before you push, run a quick mixed synthetic on A10:
```
./tools/loadtest/run_mixed.py \
  --model llama-3-8b \
  --mix 80:20 \
  --short_prompt_tokens 64 \
  --long_prompt_tokens 4096 \
  --concurrency 64 \
  --duration_s 180
```
watch TTFT p95 + “queue_time_p95”. if TTFT p95 blows up > ~15% on this change, you probably over-admitted prefill into the iteration.

Julian Moore: while you’re in there, can you add a debug log line when we *choose* to schedule prefill vs decode? doesn’t need to be a metric yet. i’m trying to make sure we can interpret traces once PR-24888 lands.

Lena Fischer: for now logs are fine. but keep it sampled; we don’t want to spam.

Marcus Reed: ok. thinking something like:
```
RW_LOG_DEBUG_SAMPLED(0.01) << "iter_plan" << " prefill=" << prefill_count << " decode=" << decode_count
```

Omar El-Sayed: also double check that request state transitions don’t happen mid-iteration. i hit a bug earlier where a request got marked DECODE before KV blocks were committed, and then decode step tried to append into uninitialized cache. easiest guard: transition to DECODE only after prefill completion callback.

Marcus Reed: where is that callback currently? i’m seeing executor returns a per-request status.

Lena Fischer: `runtime/serving/executor/executor.cc` -> `on_step_complete()` updates per-request counters. in this PR we’re moving the phase update into that path (so scheduler doesn’t guess).

Hiro Tanaka: for quick perf check on kernel thrash: if you can capture a 30s profile with Nsight Systems, look at kernel name churn. if you see attention kernels alternating each step, we’re unstable.

Grace Kim: if you don’t have Nsight handy, we have a cheap proxy metric: `runtime.kernel_autotune.reselect_count`. if it spikes after this change under mixed load, you’re flipping shapes too much.

Redwood CI Bot: buildkite #runtime / pr-24857 : running `unit` + `scheduler_regression`...

Benji Okafor: also reminder: this is behind a flag. make sure default is OFF and config validation doesn’t require the new keys.

Marcus Reed: ack. i’ll default the caps to 0 (=disabled) unless flag enabled.

Julian Moore: can you drop a note in the PR description about which Grafana panels you checked? folks keep asking during review.

Marcus Reed: will do. plan is: run mixed loadtest (80/20) on local A10, compare against baseline runtime-1.18, screenshot TTFT p95 + queue_time p95. if stable, ship.

Lena Fischer: :thumbsup: ping me on review once CI is green. biggest review point will be making sure the scheduler can’t starve decode once it’s in progress.

Marcus Reed: thanks all. pushing an update now.
